tool_input.description: Run scratch program to inspect actual ExtendedBufferedReader behavior

result:
No leftover files. The test class `ExtendedBufferedReaderAgentTest` is complete: 27 tests, 23 pass, 4 fail — each failure points to a real bug in `ExtendedBufferedReader`:

1. **`testReadAtEofDoesNotAdvancePosition`** — `read()` increments `position` even when it returns `EOF`, so the position keeps growing on every call past end-of-stream instead of staying put.
2. **`testBulkReadAtEofDoesNotChangePosition`** — `read(char[], int, int)` does `position += len`, and when `len == EOF (-1)`, this *decrements* `position` by 1 instead of leaving it unchanged.
3. **`testBulkReadLineNumberDoesNotDropWhenEofIsReached`** — the bulk `read(char[], int, int)` never increments `lineNumber` for a final, unterminated line at EOF (unlike the single-char `read()`, which does), so `getLineNumber()` correctly reports the current line while positioned on `'c'`, but drops by one once EOF is reached through a bulk read.
4. **`testBytesReadAtEofDoesNotAddBytes`** — when byte-tracking is enabled, `read()` passes the `EOF` sentinel (`-1`) into `getEncodedCharLength`, which casts it to `char` `0xFFFF` and encodes it as a real character, adding bogus bytes (3, for UTF-8) to `getBytesRead()` even though no character was actually read.
